subChunks.title: Grid Layout
subChunks.hookHtml: Flexbox is brilliant for a single row of nav links. It breaks down the moment you need both rows and columns simultaneously. CSS Grid is the two-dimensional layout system every front-end developer reaches for when building real pages — and Tailwind puts it directly in your class string.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
Grid vs Flex — choosing the right tool

The rule of thumb is simple but important:

  • One axis (a row OR a column) → use flex
  • Two axes (rows AND columns simultaneously) → use grid

A navigation bar is one axis — items flow in a single row. Use flex. A feature card grid is two axes — you care about both the columns and the rows they fill. Use grid.

Basic grid setup

class="grid grid-cols-3 gap-6"

grid enables the grid context. grid-cols-3 creates three equal-width columns (1fr 1fr 1fr under the hood). gap-6 adds spacing between all cells.

Available column counts out of the box: grid-cols-1 through grid-cols-12. There is also grid-cols-none to reset.

Arbitrary column definitions — the sidebar pattern

class="grid grid-cols-[240px_1fr] gap-0"

/* 240px_1fr becomes 240px 1fr in CSS — underscores are spaces */

Spanning columns and rows

col-span-2      /* stretch across 2 columns */
col-span-full   /* stretch to fill all columns */
col-start-2     /* start at column line 2 */
col-end-4       /* end before column line 4 */
row-span-2      /* stretch across 2 rows */

Gap control

gap-4       /* uniform gap on both axes */
gap-x-6     /* horizontal gap only */
gap-y-2     /* vertical gap only */

Alignment utilities

place-items-center   /* centre content in every cell */
items-start          /* align items at the start of their row */
justify-items-end    /* push items to the right of their column */

Common patterns

/* 3-column feature card grid */
<div class="grid grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3 gap-6">

/* Sidebar + main layout */
<div class="grid grid-cols-[240px_1fr] min-h-screen">
  <aside class="border-r border-gray-200">...</aside>
  <main class="p-8">...</main>
</div>

/* Asymmetric hero: text | image */
<div class="grid grid-cols-[1fr_2fr] gap-8 items-center">

Lyra: "Don't reach for grid for a row of buttons, a flex nav, or anything that genuinely only flows along one axis. Flex is simpler to reason about in those cases. The cognitive overhead of grid is worth it only when you're genuinely managing two dimensions."

storyBeats.speaker: Lyra the Scribe
storyBeats.text: Flex is excellent for a single hallway of doors. But a full floor plan needs two dimensions — rows and columns at once. That is what Grid gives you.

subChunks.guidedPracticeHtml:
Build a features grid — a 3-column grid of feature cards:

  • .grid-container: grid, grid-cols-3, gap-6
  • .feature-card: bg-white, p-6, rounded-xl, shadow-sm
  • .feature-icon: text-3xl, mb-4
  • .feature-title: text-lg, font-semibold, text-gray-900, mb-2
  • .feature-description: text-gray-600, text-sm, leading-relaxed

subChunks.soloPracticeHtml: Without referring to the guided practice, build a 2-column testimonial grid from scratch. Each testimonial card needs a quote text, an author name, and an author role. Apply a grid with gap-4, give each card a background, padding, and rounded corners. Add at least one col-span-2 card to span the full width.
subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain in your own words the difference between CSS Grid and Flexbox, and give a concrete example of a UI pattern where you would use each. Why doesn't flex work well for a card grid? Walk through the sidebar layout pattern using grid-cols-[240px_1fr] — what does the arbitrary value syntax do, and why are underscores used?

questions.prompt: Which Tailwind class creates a grid container with 3 equal columns?
questions.explanation: You need both grid (sets display: grid) and grid-cols-3 (sets grid-template-columns: repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr))). Neither alone is sufficient.

questions.prompt: You have a 3-column card grid and want one card to stretch across all three columns. Which class do you add to that card?
questions.explanation: col-span-full sets grid-column: 1 / -1, making the item span from the first to the last column line regardless of how many columns there are.

questions.prompt: A junior developer builds a 3-column feature section using flex flex-wrap gap-6 and gives each card w-1/3. It mostly works — but cards in the last row don't align with those above. What is the root cause and the correct fix?
options: Flexbox doesn't enforce row alignment across multiple rows — the fix is grid grid-cols-3 gap-6, which guarantees items align to the same column tracks
w-1/3 doesn't account for the gap — fix by using w-[calc(33.3%-16px)] on each card
flex-wrap causes items to lose their sizing — add flex-none to each card
The gap value is wrong — use gap-0 and add margin manually
questions.answer: Flexbox doesn't enforce row alignment across multiple rows — the fix is grid grid-cols-3 gap-6, which guarantees items align to the same column tracks
questions.explanation: This is the classic flex-wrap trap. flex-wrap with fractional widths is brittle — rounding errors cause gaps, and flex items in different rows don't share column tracks. CSS Grid solves both problems: items are placed on explicit tracks, so alignment is always consistent.
